question: Why is a measure usually better than a calculated column for something like `Net Sales per Unit`?
hint: Think when each is calculated and stored.
solution: A **calculated column** is computed row by row at refresh time and stored in the model, so it increases model size. A **measure** is calculated at query time, only for the cells shown, and uses no extra storage. Net Sales per Unit is a ratio that must be re-evaluated for every filter combination, so it must be a measure; a column would just store a number that cannot be correctly aggregated.
explanation: A calculated column is stored in the model for every row, while a measure is calculated only for the cells on screen. A ratio such as net sales per unit cannot be summed correctly from stored row values. So it must be a measure.
commonMistake: Making a column of net sales divided by units for each row, then averaging that column in a card. Rows with few units count as much as big ones, so the average differs from the true net sales per unit.

question: Your report with 24,000 sales rows and a `sale_datetime` column loads slowly after you add 5 more years of data. List four concrete things you would check or change, and how you would find the slow visual.
hint: Performance Analyzer and cardinality are the keywords.
solution: Find the slow visual with **Performance Analyzer** (View, Performance analyzer, Start recording, Refresh visuals) and look at DAX query vs visual display time. Then: (1) split `sale_datetime` into a date column and a separate time column (or drop the time) to reduce cardinality; (2) remove unused columns and tables in Power Query; (3) use a proper star schema with single-direction relationships instead of bi-directional ones; (4) replace calculated columns with measures, and use integer keys instead of text. Also reduce the number of visuals per page.
explanation: Each column with many unique values, such as a full timestamp, takes more memory in the VertiPaq engine. Splitting it into a date and a time column lowers the number of unique values. Smaller models refresh faster and open more quickly.
commonMistake: Keeping the full timestamp and all unused columns for five years. The file grows and every visual waits longer, even though the report only needs the date part.
